answer_text: As of December 31, 2024, 6.0 million premises were connected to Turkcell's fiber network, and it had a fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) network in 28 cities.

Delivery Hero treats the pre-August 2021 Spanish model as a probable risk and the post-August 2021 model as only a possible risk, and Glovo decided to move to an employment-based model in Spain from 2025.

- For the model operated by Glovo until August 2021, the risk is "more likely than not" to materialize, so appropriate provisions are reflected in the Consolidated Financial Statements (Strategic Risks, [4]).
- For Glovo Spain after August 2021, the rider risk is deemed possible but not probable, so it is disclosed as a contingency instead (Strategic Risks, [4]); this contingency ranges from approximately €440.0 to €770.0 million for social security contributions, late payment charges, fines and possible VAT claims, with no provision recognized since reclassification by Spanish courts was assessed as not probable (Contingencies, [16]; Auditor's Report, [3]).
- In December 2024, Glovo's management decided, effective 2025, to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain to avoid further legal uncertainties regarding the model in place since August 2021 (Strategic Risks, [2]; Business development by segment, [1]).
- Glovo will defend the self-employed status through all available instances and continue cooperating with the Spanish authorities, and for the pre-August 2021 proceedings it provided bank guarantees to Spanish courts in 2024 to secure claimed liabilities (Strategic Risks, [2]).

Zalando - end of 2022: 304.3m EUR committed to fulfilment centres
Zalando - end of 2024: 59.5m EUR committed to fulfilment centres

The commitment fell by 244.8m EUR (304.3m − 59.5m) between the end of 2022 and the end of 2024.
Approximately 850,000 riders worldwide delivered at least one order for Delivery Hero in 2024.

Zalando evolved Zalando Plus in 2024 from a paid membership to a free-to-join, points-based system that rewards customer loyalty for purchases and other engagement activities (e.g., subscribing to newsletters), with points unlocking four benefit levels; it was initially tested in Spain, expanded to France and Austria, and will roll out to more markets in 2025 [1][4][5][6][11]. The awards create a separate performance obligation granting a material right to customers [3]. At year-end, the report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities, which rose to 377.4m EUR (prior year: 304.6m EUR) [2][9].

Turkcell - 2G licence extension (agreed 7 April 2023): EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes); paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (down payment plus VAT) paid in Turkish Lira at TRY 1.7 billion during 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million) paid in April 2024 at TRY 1.1 billion, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.
Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension (900 MHz, six years until 30 April 2029): €120 million (excluding 18% VAT); paid in advance with a capital injection, with the extension agreement signed effective as of 27 April 2023.

Both operators agreed to the same headline extension fee of EUR 120 million, but Turkcell is paying in installments in Turkish Lira (including EUR 21.6 million VAT), whereas Vodafone Turkey paid its fee (excluding 18% VAT) upfront via a capital injection.
